# FOREGROUND SOURCING WORKSHEET

**Generated by `build_sourcing_worksheet.py` from `library/manifest.json` (seed 20260822). Do not hand-edit — regenerate.**

136 assets need real imagery. The other 9,864 are synthetic filler for scale and noise and need nothing.

These carry **every task target and every hard negative** in T0-B and T0-D. The placeholders currently in the library are stamped so they cannot be used in a real session by accident — that stamp is a guard, not an inconvenience, and it stays until an asset is genuinely replaced.

> **This worksheet is preparation, not permission.** Running the studies still needs **HG-4** (n ≥ 15 external participants). Sourcing the images needs no gate except the two judgement calls below.

## Owner decisions needed before starting

1. **Route for the 49 `people_family` assets.** Route B (staged, with consenting people) or Route C (the Owner's own photos, de-identified). C gives the most realistic library at the highest privacy cost — external strangers will look at these images in a study session. B costs more time and needs at least two people available across a staged trip.
2. **Confirm the specimen-document line.** Every `document_id` asset is sourced as a SPECIMEN or an obvious mock-up. No real identity document belonging to the Owner or to anyone else, at any point, for any reason.

## Constraints that decide whether a task is answerable at all

A miss here does not produce a worse result. It produces a task with no correct answer, and that is not visible until a participant is sitting in front of it.

Every count below is **verified against the manifest** each time this file is generated. If the library and this table ever disagree, the generator refuses to write rather than hand you a confident, wrong worksheet.

| Task | Population | Expected | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T2** | 1 | 1 | Exactly ONE photo of Ben in a white top on the Tokyo trip. If there are two, the task has no single right answer. |
| **T2** | 15 | 15 | 1 answer + 14 distractors: same person, same trip, other clothing. Otherwise “find the person” solves it without the attribute. |
| **T3** | 6 | 6 | 1 answer + 5 other receipts. Otherwise “the only receipt in the library” is the answer. |
| **T5** | 3 | 3 | The SAME recognisable bicycle in 3 different settings. Same-entity across time only works if it is visibly the same object. |
| **T6** | 12 | 12 | 1 answer + 11 pickup codes in other weeks, or the answer is not genuinely time-scoped. |
| **HARD-NEG** | 4 | 4 | The tenancy contract: 4 pages that look alike but read differently (section 9). |
| **HARD-NEG** | 4 | 4 | The meme: 4 byte-identical copies. Use a file copy, do not re-encode (section 8). |
| **HARD-NEG** | 7 | 7 | The second burst: 7 frames where frame 5 has a clearly different expression. That frame is the section 8 hard negative. |

## Recording the sources

Keep a `library/SOURCES.csv` beside the images: `asset_id,route,url_or_capture,licence,captured_by,consent`. Write it as the images are gathered, not afterwards from memory. Two things depend on it — the licence claim in the study report, and the ability to say precisely whose face is in the library if consent is ever withdrawn.
